audits.title: 514 Audit to Assess Negative Appendicectomy Rate (NAR) in Adult Patients in The Leicester Royal Infirmary (LRI)
audits.standard: National average negative appendicectomy rate of 20%
audits.other_findings: Of 318 admitted with suspected appendicitis, ultrasound visualised the appendix in 29.3% (48/164).
audits.citation: Baguley M, Palser T. 514 Audit to Assess Negative Appendicectomy Rate (NAR) in Adult Patients in The Leicester Royal Infirmary (LRI). British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab134.442.

audits.title: EP.FRI.96 Negative appendectomy rate in young females, between theory and practice. Full audit cycle
audits.standard: Accepted overall negative appendicectomy rate up to 20–25%
audits.setting: Appendicectomy cases; cohort of females aged 15–45 years

cycle1.result: Overall NAR 29%; NAR in females of child-bearing age 43.5% (156 cases, 37%).

cycle2.result: Overall NAR 25%; NAR in females of child-bearing age 37% (82 cases).

audits.other_findings: 632 cases in total, 238 females of child-bearing age; authors suggest appendicitis scores, serial examination and imaging to reduce NAR.
audits.citation: Hatem F, Mostafa S, Ross R, Chamali B, Ivanov A, Sonsale A, et al.. EP.FRI.96 Negative appendectomy rate in young females, between theory and practice. Full audit cycle. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab312.021.

audits.title: SP4.1.1 An Audit of Negative Appendicectomy Rates at the Borders General Hospital
audits.standard: 2012 National Appendicectomy Audit: negative appendicectomy rate <20%

cycle1.result: Negative appendicectomy rate 14.3% (74/518); imaged 12.8% (CT 6.3%, ultrasound 32.1%) vs no scan 17.1% (p=0.188).

audits.other_findings: NAR higher in females (18.1%) than males (11.1%, p<0.05); 34.9% had no imaging before surgery.
audits.citation: Brown J, Lennon K, Rae R, Young J. SP4.1.1 An Audit of Negative Appendicectomy Rates at the Borders General Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac247.041.

audits.title: SP4.09 A follow up audit of negative appendicectomy rates in a single site acute hospital
audits.standard: UK negative appendicectomy rate estimated at 20%; comparison with previous local study
audits.setting: Single site acute hospital, Royal Alexandra Hospital, Paisley
audits.intervention: not reported (increased preoperative cross-sectional imaging since 2019)

cycle2.result: Preoperative imaging 88% (mostly CT); NAR 3% (histology available in 84).

audits.other_findings: 22% had normal WCC and 22% normal CRP on admission; imaging and operative findings agreed on nature of appendicitis in 76%.
audits.citation: Thompson L, Kakos C, Foster A, Moug S. SP4.09 A follow up audit of negative appendicectomy rates in a single site acute hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_13). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf166.055.

audits.title: TPTh 4.15 Negative Appendicectomy Rate Audit in our Local Trust
audits.standard: Negative appendicectomy rate compared with UK rate of 20% (RIFT study 2020) and global 13%; trust requires preoperative imaging
audits.setting: Norfolk and Norwich University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: NAR 4.67% (7/150), all with preoperative imaging; NAR 11.54% in patients aged 16–25.

audits.other_findings: Previous trust audits found NAR 3.05% (2021) and 2.04% on re-audit; the rise to 4.67% was not significant (p=0.21).
audits.citation: Baxter N, Rai S, Kumar A, Macdonald-Leslie M, Hishi R, Paduraru M. TPTh 4.15 Negative Appendicectomy Rate Audit in our Local Trust. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.467.
